text: Text on a card that describes the card's effects.
An ability written with a colon, whose cost is everything before the colon.
Play or the stack; every other zone is inactive.
Next to a unit on its left, right, front or back in the same formation.
A card's elemental requirement, shown as element pips, and a player's count of non-dormant resources of an element.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an afflicting source kills one or more units, those units' controllers gain a rot."
The last step of a battle round, a priority window that follows the combat damage step.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an alluring column attacks, target enemy can't attack and must block it this combat if able."
A unit under your control in the region where the effect is happening.
A keyword that lets a unit card be played during battle with the effect "Recall target ally, put me into their position in play."
To put a mod onto a card, a special action that is not playing a card.
A player setup, typically 2v1, in which the single player takes 1 or 2 turns before the other two begin.
The first step of a battle, in which the attacking player declares its attacking formation.
The priority window that follows the declaration of an attack, in the region attacked.
Bringing units, and the spell tokens that travel with them, into a neighbouring enemy region for battle.
A quality a card can have, printed on its type line, that changes how it engages in combat.
A modification that adds the text after a card's augment symbol to the card it is applied to.
A client preference that passes priority for a player only in a window where passing is the only thing they could do.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two."
The part of a card that offers another way to play it, for a cost of its own, as Ambush and Prophecy do.
A timing keyword: a card with Battle can be played only while its player is in battle with another player.
The second phase of the turn, and its only interactive one.
One of the two attacks of a 1v1 or team battle phase: the initiative team's attack, then the counterattack.
A player's discard pile.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Damage dealt by a blessed source causes its controller to gain that much life."
The second step of a battle, in which the defending player may place its units in front of the attacking formation.
The priority window that follows the declaration of blocks.
How a player who has been attacked defends, by placing units in front of the attacking formation.
A client preference with which the client never finishes the haste step for the player.
A non-combat attribute printed on spell tokens: casting one casts every spell token of the same name its controller has in that region at the same time.
A public zone of each player's, beside the hand, the bin and the deck; to cache a card is to put it there.
A physical Algomancy card, one with an Algomancy card back; a token is not a card.
To play a spell; casting a spell is playing it.
A chess clock a game may be played with, in which each player has a bank of time.
One file of the battle line: the attacking units in it and the defending units placed in front of it.
An attribute printed in gold; units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes.
The damage columns deal to each other and to players in the combat damage step.
The step of a battle in which the units in formation deal combat damage.
What is used to choose which cards are in a game, shown by the colour of the set symbol.
To end the game as a loss, in the same way as being eliminated.
Not defined by these rules: the old rules glossary's mechanic that created a spell token to be cast at a set time, which no current card prints.

usedBy.quote: Conjure is a mechanic that creates a spell token that is cast at a specific time.

text: A game mode in which each player brings their own deck, built before the game, and plays from it.
An effect that changes the game for a period of time rather than once.
The player who controls a card, who may differ from its owner.
A copy of a spell is a new effect on the stack, not played; a unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text.
Something a player must pay to do something: to play a card, to apply a mod, or to activate an ability.
The part of a card that shows its mana cost.
The non-initiative team's attack in a battle phase with two battle rounds.
The old rules glossary's word for what these rules call a unit.
A format for large groups in which players draft decks before the game and then play constructed matches.
What a source deals to a unit or a player: marked on a unit, and lost as life by a player.
One of the three parts of the combat damage step, taken in order: the Swift sub-step, the normal sub-step and the Sluggish sub-step.
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit."
A counter a player has, paid off at 1 mana each at the end of that player's resource step.
The face-down pile that cards are drawn from and that packs are dealt from.
The second of a unit's stats: how much damage it can take before it dies.
To remove a unit from play into the bin, as when a unit dies.
The last phase of each turn, in which players build up their forces for the next.
What a unit does whenever it leaves play, by any route.
Not defined by these rules: an attribute the old rules glossary names without defining it, which no current card prints.

usedBy.quote: Things like Deadly, Flying, Poisonous, Electric and Devastating.

text: To put a card from a hand into the bin.
Face down: every resource enters play dormant, and activating it turns it face up (active).
The step of the planning phase in which, in a live draft, each player combines their hand with their pack and chooses which cards to keep in hand.
The step of the planning phase in which each player draws 2 cards.
Each opponent in the region where the effect happens.
Each player in the region where the effect happens.
Anything on the stack.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Excess damage from electric sources can be directed to an adjacent unit, recursively."
Out of the game: a player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated.
A special step after deployment finishes, in which abilities that trigger "at the end of turn" trigger.
A unit not under your control in the region where the effect is happening.
To take a card out of the game, to the erased pile.
The zone where a card goes when an effect erases it.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Evasive units require two blockers."
For Piercing, the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage.
A word printed in four senses, each read from its card.
To turn a resource sideways for 1 mana, once per turn, to pay a mana cost.
An attribute: a Feeble unit can't block.
When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other.
What an effect does if, as it resolves, it has lost all of its targets: it does nothing.
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units."
The placement of a player's units when they attack or block: an attacking or a defending formation.
A player setup (FFA) in which every player plays for themselves.
A client mode, held with the Control key, in which the client gives a player every stop.
Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.
A modification, marked by the graft symbol, that combines several effects under a single cause.
The attacking units of one column, or its blocking units, which deal their combat damage together as one source.
The zone of a player's own cards, which each player has and which is hidden from the other players.
A timing keyword: a card with Haste can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment.
The last step of the planning phase, in which players may play only haste cards.
A part of the turn in which both players act at once and neither sees what the other does until both are done.
The card a mod is applied to and becomes part of.
A card that belongs to two elements.
What one player has in each turn; in a 1v1 game the initiative player acts first.
The marker of which player has the initiative, passed clockwise when the turn is over; it is not a token.
A card with which players declare attacks in free-for-all, all at the same time.
An attribute whose reminder text begins "Invert the stat changes of inverted units."
A verb that card text uses with a fixed game meaning.
What a unit was at the instant it left play.
One learner against the Tutorial Bot in one continuous game, with lessons shown as each rule first matters.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Any combat damage from a lethal unit will kill a player."
What each player has, starting at 30; a player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated.
A game mode in which the players share one deck and draft cards from it during the game.
The number of resources a player must expend to play a card, shown in its cost orb.
A modification: a card that is applied to another card instead of being played.
An attribute whose reminder text begins "You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played."
To remove an effect from the stack: a negated effect is removed at once, when the effect that negates it resolves.
An attribute printed in purple, such as Burst and Unstable, that describes a card and generally has nothing to do with combat.
All damage other than combat damage.
Any effect that is not a spell effect.
The [once] keyword: an ability marked [once] can be activated or triggered only once per turn.
A question the game is waiting on a player to answer, which they must answer, or concede, before taking any other action.
The player whose card it is; a card's owner never changes.
In live draft, each player's face-down pile of 10 cards dealt from the deck, which that player drafts from.
One of the four parts of a turn: the planning, battle, regroup and deployment phases.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller."
The element marks with a card's cost, which are its affinity requirement and not part of its cost.
The first phase of the turn, in which players prepare for the turn ahead.
The zone of the units, resources and tokens on the table.
What is done to units and spells, from whatever zone: meeting the card's affinity requirement, paying its mana cost and selecting its targets.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Poisonous sources damage units in the form of -1/-1 counters."
The first of a unit's stats: how much damage it deals in combat.
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Powerful sources deal double damage."
An effect that prevents damage that would be dealt; it is not a replacement effect.
The ability to take game actions such as playing cards or activating abilities.
A sequence in which the players (or teams) each receive priority in order.
A resource with no element, which gives no affinity.
A keyword printed on a card's banner as a cost and a condition.
To pay the cost on a card's prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes."
Not defined by these rules: the 2023 Rulebook's attribute that dealt combat damage first and could block fliers, which no current card prints.

usedBy.quote: Spike has the “Ranged” attribute, which allows it to deal combat damage first and block fliers.

text: An attribute whose reminder text begins "When a reaping source kills one or more units, draw a card."
To put a card into a hand.
The playback each player is shown of what the other did in the haste step or in deployment.
To put a card on the bottom of the deck, past the deck's mark, into the recycle pile.
The cards past the deck's mark, where a card put on the bottom of the deck goes.
The first step of the planning phase, in which each player's expended resources refresh.
Where all gameplay takes place; there is one region for each player.
The global step, once battle has ended in every region, that resets the game between battles.
Italic text that restates what an attribute or keyword does.
An ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead".
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a resonant source deals damage to a unit, it deals that much damage to that unit's controller."
A source of mana, which a player needs to play cards.
The step of the planning phase in which players create and activate resources.
Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit.
A counter a player has, which deals that player damage equal to it at the start of each deployment phase.
For a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin.
A moment at which the game makes state checks, such as the end of every action.
A resource of its own kind, which pays one generic mana once activated.
A defending unit placed blocking where no attacker is.
A variant of constructed in which each player picks a single card and their deck is 30 copies of it.
The old rules glossary's name for the place where attackers meet defenders, one per player; the current term is region.

usedBy.quote: Each of these locations is called a Skirmish.

text: A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last."
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Sneaky units can't be blocked if attacking alone."
The thing that deals damage.
A card type that provides a one-time effect.
An effect that is a spell: a spell, a spell unit or a spell token on the stack, or an ambush.
A spell that an effect creates directly into play, which its controller may cast from play.
A card that is both a spell and a unit.
The zone where cards being played, and abilities, wait to resolve, the last one put there resolving first.
Pass through stack or Pass all: a promise the client keeps on a player's behalf in later windows.
A check the game itself makes at safe points, in which every unit that should be dead dies.
An ability that states a change its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play.
A unit's two numbers, printed power/defense.
An effect that makes a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both.
A word of the type line other than its markers and its card type, such as Whale.
A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first."
Something a card or ability chooses, with the word "target", to receive its actions.
A player setup in which two teams play against each other, 2v2 or 3v3.
An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a thieving source deals combat damage to an opponent, draw a card."
When an effect began to apply.
An icon in the top right corner of a card that changes when, and how, the card can be played.
A unit or a spell that an effect creates directly into play; a token is not a card.
An attribute: a Tough unit's defense is doubled.
To turn a card in play to its other face up; it stays the same unit and does not leave play.
What happens to a card that enters a bin from any zone except the stack.
An ability that happens when something else takes place.
The global cycle of four phases that every player goes through together.
The line of a card that describes what the card is.
An attribute: an Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it.
A card type that, once it enters play, stays there until something removes it; units attack and defend.
A unit that an effect creates, whether or not the effect calls it a token.
A non-combat attribute: an Unstable card that would enter a bin from an active zone is erased instead.
A timing icon: a Virus card can also be applied as an augment from the hand during battle.
An attribute: a Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage that would be dealt to it.
A number that the card defines.
On a card, the controller of the effect.
One of the places a card can be: the deck, the hand, the cache, play, the bin, the stack, the erased pile, the recycle pile and the pack.
